title: EchoWM: A World Model You Can Walk Into and Hear
hook: Most world models generate silent video. EchoWM generates 720p video plus environmental sound, music, and speech, and lets you navigate it continuously.
key_points: An omnimodal world model that jointly generates 720p video, environmental sound, music, and speech while responding to continuous navigation.
Interaction is organized around camera intent: observer motion in first-person scenes, learned camera-character dynamics in third-person ones.
Discrete commands and continuous poses both map to one shared metric-scale relative 6-DoF trajectory.
Dataset-level calibration preserves motion magnitude across heterogeneous training sources.
Progressive training followed by autoregressive post-training gives long-horizon generation with audio staying synchronized.
content_html: Interactive world models — generative systems you can move through rather than merely watch — have mostly been silent. Zhang and colleagues present EchoWM, which generates 720p video together with environmental sound, music, and speech while responding to continuous navigation input.
extra_html:
Controlling it

The interaction abstraction is camera intent. In first-person scenes the camera is the observer, so intent is straightforwardly where you move. In third-person scenes the relationship between the camera and the character is learned from data instead of being handled by a view-specific controller. Both discrete commands and continuous poses are projected onto a shared metric-scale relative 6-DoF trajectory, and dataset-level calibration keeps motion magnitude consistent when training data comes from very different sources.

Making it last

Joint audio-visual generation under trajectory control is trained with a complementary data engine, progressive training, and then autoregressive post-training aimed at long horizons. The authors report strong trajectory following and visual quality on public world-model benchmarks across first- and third-person interaction, with sound and speech staying synchronized as generation extends — the part that usually drifts first.

related.title: AlayaWorld: An Open-Source Framework for Playable Video Worlds
related.hook: Building a game world the old way means authoring every asset by hand. AlayaWorld generates it live instead — combat, spell-casting, monster summoning — and open-sources the whole pipeline.

related.title: MIRA: A Multiplayer World Model for Rocket League
related.hook: Single-player world models treat other agents as scenery. This one, trained on 10,000 hours of Rocket League, tracks four players' independent actions at once — and stays coherent for hours.

related.title: World Models Lack a Persistent State
related.hook: Today's video world models render great frames but treat the world like a tracking shot: look away and back, and off-screen events freeze instead of running on — the moon keeps orbiting unwatched.

flashcards.prompt: What does organizing interaction around 'camera intent' let EchoWM avoid?
flashcards.back_html: Separate view-specific controllers — first-person camera intent means observer motion, and third-person camera-character dynamics are learned from data instead of hand-built.

flashcards.prompt: Why map both discrete commands and continuous poses to a shared metric-scale 6-DoF trajectory?

choices.text: So heterogeneous control inputs and datasets share one consistent motion representation
To reduce the video resolution needed for training
Because 6-DoF poses cannot be generated directly
To let the model skip audio generation when navigating

flashcards.explanation_html: A single relative trajectory space, plus dataset-level calibration that preserves motion magnitude, lets varied control schemes and data sources train one controller.

flashcards.prompt: What makes EchoWM 'omnimodal' rather than just a video world model?
flashcards.back_html: It generates environmental sound, music, and speech jointly with the video, and keeps them synchronized over long-horizon autoregressive rollouts.
